messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: 我想在 r/WarriorCats 发一个提问帖，问问大家的看法。
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit, question post:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about that.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest skies, and it would be hard / not worth it to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wanted to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it’s onlynatural that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or does StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t go for another try on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
The part: "hard / not worth it"
What is wrong with it: 'Hard' says StarClan could not reach the kittypet, while 'not worth it' says StarClan chose not to bother. These claims lead to different readings of Ravenpaw's explanation and the reader cannot tell which the writer means.
What they mean (confirmed by them): Reaching the kittypet was physically or magically hard.
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "physically or magically hard"
Words they already have as hints: physically, magically, tough
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"This slot needs a short description of how difficult the trip was, placed right after \"would be\" so it works as one quality. Start with one kind of difficulty, then add the second kind with a small connecting word, and let the final word of the description carry the main emphasis.","example":"The climb was [physically] [or] mentally [hard] for beginners."}
